title: Sodium Metal in Water – Vigorous Bubbling & pH Change
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D chemistry lab simulation of dropping sodium metal into water, using Three.js (via CDN) and GLTFLoader.

## Asset Loading
- Load 'DamagedHelmet.glb' and repurpose it as a corroded sodium metal sample holder / protective shield mounted on the lab bench behind the beaker. Scale it to ~0.4 and position it at (-2, 1.2, 0). It represents the protective fume-hood visor.
- Load 'BoxAnimated.glb' and repurpose it as the sodium metal chunk container (a storage box). Scale it to ~0.5 and position it at (2, 0.8, 0). Play its built-in animation when the user opens the container. The sodium chunk is extracted from this box.
- Both models must be loaded via THREE.GLTFLoader from a CDN. Track loading in window.__3D_STATE__.assetsLoaded (increment for each; final value 2).

## Scene Setup
- Renderer: antialias, sRGB output, toneMapping ACESFilmic, 800x600 or fullscreen.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 6) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- Lights: HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x444444, 1.0) + DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.5) at (3, 8, 5) with shadow.
- Lab bench: a Box geometry (6x0.2x3) at y=0, brown material (#8B4513).
- Glass beaker: a transparent CylinderGeometry (radius 0.8, height 2, openEnded false) at (0, 1, 0) with transparent blue-tinted glass material (opacity 0.3). Inside, a water body: another cylinder (radius 0.75, height 1.2) with blue semi-transparent material at y=0.7.
- Sodium chunk: a small IcosahedronGeometry (radius 0.15) with shiny metallic silver material, initially hidden (visible=false), stored conceptually inside the BoxAnimated container.
- pH indicator strip: a thin BoxGeometry (0.6x0.05x0.1) at (1.5, 0.15, 1.2) on the bench. Its color starts green (#00AA00, pH~7) and shifts to deep purple (#6600CC, pH~14) as the reaction proceeds.
- Bubble particle system: create a pool of 80 small sphere meshes (radius 0.02-0.05, white/translucent) initially invisible. When reaction is active, animate them rising from the sodium chunk's position upward through the water with random lateral drift, recycling when they exit the water surface.
- Temperature gauge: a DOM overlay div showing 'Temp: 20.0°C' that rises during reaction.
- Hydrogen gas cloud: a group of 5 semi-transparent white spheres above the beaker opening that fade in during vigorous reaction phase, representing H2 gas.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose ALL of the following:
- assetsLoaded: number (0->1->2 as models load)
- containerOpen: boolean (false initially)
- sodiumDropped: boolean (false initially)
- sodiumInWater: boolean (false initially)
- reactionStarted: boolean
- reactionPhase: string ('idle' | 'mild' | 'vigorous' | 'explosive' | 'complete')
- reactionTime: number (seconds since reaction started, 0 initially)
- pH: number (starts at 7.0, rises toward 14.0 during reaction)
- temperature: number (starts at 20.0, rises during reaction)
- bubbleCount: number (active visible bubbles at any moment)
- hydrogenVisible: boolean (H2 cloud visible)
- sodiumRadius: number (starts at 0.15, shrinks to 0 as sodium dissolves)
- sodiumPosition: {x, y, z} (track sodium chunk world position)
- waterColor: string (hex, starts '#4488FF', shifts to '#88AAFF' as NaOH forms)
- pHStripColor: string (hex color of the indicator strip)
- reactionEnergy: number (cumulative energy released in kJ, starts 0, max ~368)
- paused: boolean (false)
- undoStack: array of snapshot objects
- canUndo: boolean

## Interactions
1. CLICK on the BoxAnimated model (raycast): opens the container (plays its animation), sets containerOpen=true, makes sodium chunk visible floating above the box.
2. KEYBOARD 'D' (drop): if containerOpen && !sodiumDropped, animates the sodium chunk in an arc from above the box to above the beaker, then drops it into the water. Sets sodiumDropped=true. When it hits water surface (y ~ 1.3), set sodiumInWater=true and reactionStarted=true.
3. REACTION SIMULATION (automatic after sodiumInWater):
   - Phase 1 'mild' (0-3s): pH rises 7->9, temp 20->35, bubbleCount ~10-20, sodium floats on water surface bobbing, sodiumRadius shrinks slowly.
   - Phase 2 'vigorous' (3-7s): pH 9->12, temp 35->65, bubbleCount 30-50, sodium moves erratically on surface, hydrogenVisible=true, sodiumRadius shrinks faster.
   - Phase 3 'explosive' (7-9s): pH 12->13.5, temp 65->95, bubbleCount 50-80, bright yellow-orange flash (point light burst), sodium nearly gone.
   - Phase 4 'complete' (>9s): pH settles at ~14, temp cools slowly toward 40, bubbleCount->0, sodiumRadius=0 (dissolved), reactionPhase='complete'.
   - reactionEnergy accumulates proportionally, reaching ~368 kJ at complete.
   - Water color shifts gradually. pH strip color shifts from green through yellow, blue, to purple.
4. KEYBOARD 'P': toggle pause. When paused, all animation freezes, paused=true.
5. KEYBOARD 'U': undo �� restore the last snapshot from undoStack (snapshots are pushed every 2 seconds during reaction and before each user action). Restores pH, temperature, reactionTime, reactionPhase, sodiumRadius, etc. Sets canUndo based on stack length.
6. KEYBOARD 'R': full reset – everything back to initial state, sodium hidden, container closed, pH=7, temp=20, reactionPhase='idle'.
7. DOM BUTTON 'Add Phenolphthalein': adds a pink tint to the water when pH > 8.2 (the real indicator transition). Toggled by a button in the HUD. Track as window.__3D_STATE__.phenolphthaleinAdded (boolean).

## HUD / UI
- Top-left overlay: 'pH: {value}', 'Temp: {value}°C', 'Phase: {phase}', 'Energy: {value} kJ'
- Button: 'Add Phenolphthalein'
- Button: 'Reset'
- Small text: 'Controls: Click box to open | D=Drop sodium | P=Pause | U=Undo | R=Reset'

## Physics Constraints
- Energy conservation: reactionEnergy must monotonically increase (never decrease except on undo/reset) and not exceed 368 kJ.
- pH must stay in [0, 14] range at all times.
- Temperature must never be NaN or negative.
- Sodium radius must monotonically decrease during reaction (never increase except undo/reset) and stay >= 0.
- Bubble positions must stay within beaker cylinder bounds (radius < 0.75, y between 0.1 and 1.3).
- Sodium position while floating must stay within beaker radius and near water surface.
physics_constraints: Energy released monotonically increases to max ~368 kJ (Na + H2O -> NaOH + 0.5H2). pH bounded [0,14], monotonically non-decreasing during reaction. Temperature non-negative, never NaN. Sodium radius monotonically non-increasing during reaction, bounded [0, 0.15]. Bubbles confined within beaker geometry. Conservation: total Na mass = dissolved NaOH mass (tracked via radius shrinkage).
